evals.prompt: We need to explore all viable architectures for a home-energy product — parameters like storage, control, ownership model, pricing. Help me map the solution space and prune the impossible combos.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Defines 4-8 MECE parameters and 2-6 discrete values each, and states the raw configuration count as the product of the value counts; Performs a pairwise cross-consistency assessment: each excluded value pair is typed logical / empirical / normative and carries a one-line reason; Reports the internally consistent count and the reduction achieved (raw vs consistent), reproduced with scripts/morph.py; Shortlists and names interesting configurations, saying what would make each work.
expectations: Defines 4-8 MECE parameters and 2-6 discrete values each, and states the raw configuration count as the product of the value counts
Performs a pairwise cross-consistency assessment: each excluded value pair is typed logical / empirical / normative and carries a one-line reason
Reports the internally consistent count and the reduction achieved (raw vs consistent), reproduced with scripts/morph.py
Shortlists and names interesting configurations, saying what would make each work

evals.prompt: Run a Zwicky box / morphological analysis on our sensor-platform design options — I want the full box, then a cross-consistency assessment so we only look at combinations that can actually coexist.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Builds the morphological box (parameters as columns, values beneath) and prints the raw count; Assesses every cross-parameter value pair, leaving no block un-assessed (cca reports complete); Lists the consistent configurations, optionally filtered by a driver value; Does not read causation into the matrix — pairs are judged for compatibility only.
expectations: Builds the morphological box (parameters as columns, values beneath) and prints the raw count
Assesses every cross-parameter value pair, leaving no block un-assessed (cca reports complete)
Lists the consistent configurations, optionally filtered by a driver value
Does not read causation into the matrix — pairs are judged for compatibility only

evals.prompt: How many internally consistent business-model configurations exist here? We have five dimensions (customer segment, revenue mechanism, channel, ownership, pricing) with 3-4 options each and a list of combinations we already know are contradictory.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Computes the raw count (product of option counts) and the count of internally consistent configurations after applying the stated exclusions; Asks for or records a reason and a type for each contradiction rather than accepting bare exclusions; Reports raw vs consistent with the reduction percentage and reconciles the number with the companion tool.
expectations: Computes the raw count (product of option counts) and the count of internally consistent configurations after applying the stated exclusions
Asks for or records a reason and a type for each contradiction rather than accepting bare exclusions
Reports raw vs consistent with the reduction percentage and reconciles the number with the companion tool

evals.prompt: We have decided to move all customer support to an AI agent next quarter. Map the second-order and third-order consequences of that decision — the ripple effects and unintended consequences.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Does not build a parameter box or count configurations; Places the decision at the centre and generates first-, second- and third-order consequence rings (futures-wheel behaviour).
expectations: Does not build a parameter box or count configurations
Places the decision at the centre and generates first-, second- and third-order consequence rings (futures-wheel behaviour)

evals.prompt: Build me a 2x2 scenario matrix for the European EV-charging market over the next five years — pick the two most uncertain drivers and narrate the four plausible futures.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Does not enumerate a multi-parameter configuration space or run a cross-consistency assessment; Selects two critical uncertainties, constructs the 2x2 matrix and narrates four scenarios (scenario-planning behaviour).
expectations: Does not enumerate a multi-parameter configuration space or run a cross-consistency assessment
Selects two critical uncertainties, constructs the 2x2 matrix and narrates four scenarios (scenario-planning behaviour)
